banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.name: Lang Dong peanut rice cake
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.serving_basis: Four servings of sliced rice cake with fermented soybean dipping sauce.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.description: Lang Dong peanut rice cake is ivory-white, soft and chewy, with roasted peanuts and the gentle alkaline note of nuoc nang. Bep Viet adapts the stirring method for rice flour at home and recommends only food-grade nuoc nang; do not make an ash solution yourself.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.finished_dish: The rice cake is smooth and chewy, cut into neat pieces with peanuts evenly distributed throughout. It tastes gently of rice and peanuts, with a subtle note from nuoc nang.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.serving: Let the rice cake cool slightly, then cut it into bite-size pieces. Serve with fermented soybean dip; add fresh herbs if desired.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.image_alt: Lang Dong peanut rice cake, ivory-white slices with whole peanuts, served with a small bowl of fermented soybean dip.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.time_note: About 1 hour 30 minutes, not including the time for the rice cake to cool completely.
tips: Stir the powder in cold water before turning on the stove to limit clumping.
Only use water of food origin; Do not use self-filtered ash water or unlabeled chemicals.
Stir continuously over low heat until the dough is clear and the membrane is stretched; The cake will thicken as it cools.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Choose fine, fresh flour; Sieve before use.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use cool water to make the batter.

ingredients.name: Shelled peanuts
ingredients.notes: Soak for 30 minutes, boil until tender and drain.

ingredients.name: Food-grade nuoc nang (traditional alkaline water)
ingredients.notes: Use only a clearly labeled food-grade product. If unavailable, omit it, but the rice cake will have a different flavor and texture.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust or decrease according to the saltiness of the accompanying soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Apply thinly to the mold to make it easier to remove the cake.

ingredients.name: Fermented soybean sauce
ingredients.notes: Serve as a dip and taste it before adding any seasoning.

preparation_steps: Soak the peanuts in clean water for 30 minutes, rinse, then boil until tender but still whole. Drain.
Whisk the rice flour, salt and water together in a cold pot until smooth. Let the batter rest for 30 minutes, then stir again.
Lightly oil a mold or heatproof tray. Measure the food-grade nuoc nang and prepare the fermented soybean dip.
cooking_steps: Set the pot over low heat. Stir continuously, scraping the bottom and sides, until the batter begins to thicken.
Add the food-grade nuoc nang and keep stirring for 20–25 minutes, until the cake mixture turns translucent, thick and glossy and no longer tastes of raw flour.
Fold in the boiled peanuts and stir for 2 minutes. Transfer the mixture to the mold, smooth the top and let it cool until set.
Cut the rice cake into bite-size pieces and serve with fermented soybean dip. If the dip is salty, thin it with a little warm water and taste again.
banh-duc-lac-lang-dong.media_alt_text: Lang Dong peanut rice cake, ivory-white slices with whole peanuts, served with a small bowl of fermented soybean dip.

che-kho-nam-dinh.name: Nam Dinh che kho
aliases: Nam Dinh Festival Mung Bean Cake
che-kho-nam-dinh.serving_basis: Six servings of thick mung bean che kho, molded and topped with toasted sesame.
che-kho-nam-dinh.description: Nam Dinh che kho is a thick mung bean sweet, molded and served for festivals and holidays. Despite the word che, it is closer to a soft cake than a liquid dessert. Bep Viet keeps the mung bean, ginger and toasted sesame notes while moderating the sugar for a home-sized batch.
che-kho-nam-dinh.finished_dish: A golden, smooth mung bean sweet with a pleasantly firm, chewy texture, fragrant with ginger and finished with toasted sesame.
che-kho-nam-dinh.serving: Let the mung bean sweet cool in the mold, then cut it into small pieces. Serve with hot tea after a meal or include it on a festival offering tray.
che-kho-nam-dinh.image_alt: A golden molded Nam Dinh mung bean cake topped with toasted sesame and fine strands of ginger.
che-kho-nam-dinh.time_note: About 4 hours 10 minutes, including soaking time; the beans can be soaked overnight.
tips: Soak the mung beans until plump and steam them fully so the finished paste is smooth rather than grainy.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously and scraping the pan so the mung bean paste does not scorch.
You can reduce the sugar slightly, but cook the paste until thick enough to hold its shape when cool.

ingredients.name: Split, hulled mung beans
ingredients.notes: Pick them clean, soak them in water for 3-4 hours and then drain.

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.notes: Reduce to 120 g for a less-sweet result.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel, pound or chop very finely.

ingredients.name: White sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Toast until fragrant, then cool.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a small pinch to balance the sweetness.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use only enough water for steaming; do not mix it into the mung bean paste after steaming.

preparation_steps: Rinse the mung beans until the water runs clear. Soak for 3–4 hours, rinse again and drain.
Peel and finely mince the ginger. Toast the sesame in a dry pan until fragrant, then let it cool.
Set up a steamer and small mold. Line the mold with food-safe film or coat it lightly with oil.
cooking_steps: Steam the mung beans for 25–30 minutes until tender. While still hot, mash or blend them into a smooth paste.
Put the mung bean paste, sugar, salt and ginger in a heavy-bottomed pan. Cook over low heat, stirring until evenly combined.
Continue cooking for 15–20 minutes, until the paste is thick and pliable, gathers into a mass and briefly exposes the pan after each stroke.
Press the hot mung bean paste into the mold and smooth the top. Let it cool completely, unmold, sprinkle with toasted sesame and serve.
che-kho-nam-dinh.media_alt_text: A golden molded Nam Dinh mung bean cake topped with toasted sesame and fine strands of ginger.

mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.name: Mekong-Style Vegetarian Mam Kho
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.serving_basis: Four servings of vegetables, mushrooms and tofu braised in a savory broth, served with rice or vermicelli.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.description: Mekong-style vegetarian mam kho simmers vegetables, mushrooms and tofu in a savory plant-based broth fragrant with lemongrass and lightly enriched with coconut milk. Bep Viet's fully plant-based version is a spoonable stew for rice, distinct from thick vegetarian kho quet dipping sauce.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.finished_dish: The amber-brown broth balances savory and sweet notes; tofu is tender and well-seasoned, while the vegetables stay intact and the mushrooms remain juicy.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.serving: Spoon the braising broth and vegetables into a warm serving bowl. Serve with steamed rice or fresh vermicelli, with fresh greens, chili and lime on the side.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.image_alt: Mekong-style vegetarian mam kho in a clay pot, with tofu, eggplant, mushrooms and okra in a rich brown broth.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.time_note: About 55 minutes; prepare the vegetables ahead to shorten active cooking time.
tips: Choose a fully plant-based fermented seasoning and check the label to make sure it contains no fish.
Lightly fry the tofu first to firm its surface, then braise it; handle gently to keep the pieces intact.
Add the vegetables that need longer cooking first, then the tofu and coconut milk. Taste before adding salt.

ingredients.name: Firm white tofu
ingredients.notes: Drain the water and cut into large square pieces.

ingredients.name: Eggplant
ingredients.notes: Cut into chunks, soak briefly in lightly salted water and drain.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the stems and rinse; halve any large mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Okra
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut diagonally into short pieces.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the eyes and cut into small pieces.

ingredients.name: Plant-based fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a fully plant-based brand and season gradually, as salt levels vary.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Add near the end for a light, creamy richness.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass stalks
ingredients.notes: Bruise and cut into lengths; mince a little for sautéing if desired.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Mince; omit if you avoid alliums in your vegetarian diet.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust the amount to the saltiness of the plant-based fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use to lightly fry the tofu and sauté the lemongrass.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to adjust the consistency of the braising broth.

ingredients.name: Red chilli
ingredients.notes: Remove the seeds for mild heat, or omit the chili altogether.

preparation_steps: Press and drain the tofu, then cut it into bite-size pieces. Prepare the eggplant, straw mushrooms, okra and pineapple; rinse and drain.
Bruise the lemongrass and cut it into lengths. Mince the shallots if using. Stir the plant-based fish sauce, water and sugar together until dissolved.
Pan-fry the tofu in a little oil until lightly golden on all sides. Remove and drain.
cooking_steps: Heat the pot and sauté the lemongrass and shallots in oil until fragrant. Add the pineapple and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Pour in the plant-based fish sauce mixture and bring it to a gentle simmer. Add the eggplant and mushrooms, partially cover and braise for about 10 minutes.
Add the okra and fried tofu. Lower the heat and braise for 8–10 minutes, gently shaking the pot now and then instead of stirring vigorously.
Stir in the coconut milk and taste for balance. Simmer for 2 minutes, then turn off the heat, garnish with chili if desired and serve hot.
mam-kho-chay-mien-tay.media_alt_text: Mekong-style vegetarian mam kho in a clay pot, with tofu, eggplant, mushrooms and okra in a rich brown broth.

bun-hen-mai-xa.name: Mai Xa bun hen
aliases: Mai Xa Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli
Quang Tri Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli
bun-hen-mai-xa.serving_basis: Four bowls of Mai Xa mixed vermicelli with chat chat clams, hot broth, greens, peanuts and toasted rice cracker.
bun-hen-mai-xa.description: Mai Xa bun hen is known for brackish-water chat chat, a small mollusk related to clams. Bep Viet adapts it as mixed vermicelli with soy sauce, chili sauce, herbs and peanuts, with a little cooking broth on the side; it does not use the fermented shrimp paste and taro stems found in some Hue bun hen versions.
bun-hen-mai-xa.finished_dish: A bowl of vermicelli topped with sweet, savory chat chat clams, toasted peanuts, crisp greens and warming ginger, with a mild soy-and-chili dressing.
bun-hen-mai-xa.serving: Divide the rice vermicelli among bowls, then top with chat chat clams, herbs and peanuts. Break the rice cracker over each bowl. Serve soy-chili sauce and hot clam broth separately.
bun-hen-mai-xa.image_alt: Mai Xa vermicelli with chat chat clams, roasted peanuts, herbs and toasted rice cracker, served with soy-chili sauce on the side.
bun-hen-mai-xa.time_note: About 1 hour 25 minutes, including soaking time for clams in their shells.
tips: Use cleaned chat chat clams from a reputable seller. If buying them in their shells, soak them and change the water to release sand.
Avoid boiling the clams after their shells have just opened, or the meat may turn tough.
Serve the soy sauce and chili sauce separately so the clams' natural sweetness remains prominent.

ingredients.notes: Buy live chat chat clams from a traceable source. Soak and rinse them repeatedly to release sand.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch in boiling water, then drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice half for the broth and mince the rest.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use in a separate dressing and season to taste.

ingredients.name: Chili sauce
ingredients.notes: Serve on the side so everyone can adjust the heat.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush coarsely; do not grind to a powder.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Use cilantro, basil and young mustard greens if available; rinse and dry thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Toasted rice crackers
ingredients.notes: Grilled until crispy, broken into bite-sized pieces.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use to sauté the shallots and stir-fry the clams.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the broth after straining.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add hot water during cooking if needed.

preparation_steps: Soak the clams in clean water for 30 minutes, change the water once and rinse them several times. If using cleaned clam meat, thaw it in the refrigerator.
Rinse the herbs and dry them thoroughly. Slice the ginger and mince part of it; thinly slice the shallots and lightly crush the roasted peanuts.
Briefly blanch the rice vermicelli according to the seller's instructions, then drain. Toast the rice cracker until crisp and break it into pieces.
cooking_steps: Bring the water and sliced ginger to a boil. Add the clams and stir gently until their shells just open. Remove them and strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve.
Remove the clam meat from the shells if needed. Sauté the shallots in oil, add minced ginger and clam meat, stir-fry for 2–3 minutes, then season lightly with salt.
Mix the soy sauce and chili sauce with a little clam broth. Adjust the seasoning so it is gently salty and spicy without masking the clams' sweetness.
Divide the rice vermicelli among bowls and top with the clams, herbs and roasted peanuts. Break the rice cracker over each bowl and serve with soy-chili sauce and hot clam broth on the side.
bun-hen-mai-xa.media_alt_text: Mai Xa vermicelli with chat chat clams, roasted peanuts, herbs and toasted rice cracker, served with soy-chili sauce on the side.

canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.name: Phu Quoc Tram Mushroom Soup
aliases: Phu Quoc Tram Mushroom and Shrimp Soup
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.serving_basis: Four bowls of tram mushroom and shrimp soup, served hot with rice.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.description: Phu Quoc tram mushroom soup evokes the forest mushroom season after the rains, with a gentle initial bitterness and a sweet finish. Bep Viet adapts it with shrimp for a light broth and uses safely prepared mushrooms. Phu Quoc is now part of An Giang Province, while the familiar dish name retains its local identity.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.finished_dish: The clear broth is gently sweet from shrimp; tram mushrooms hold their shape and lend a characteristic mild bitterness, finished with scallions and cilantro.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.serving: Ladle the hot soup into bowls and finish with scallions, cilantro and a little pepper. Serve with steamed rice and enjoy the mushrooms' gentle bitterness and sweet finish.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.image_alt: A bowl of clear Phu Quoc tram mushroom soup with purple-brown mushrooms, fresh shrimp, scallions and cilantro.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.time_note: About 45 minutes when using cleaned mushrooms; prep time depends on the type of mushroom.
tips: Use only tram mushrooms identified and prepared by a trusted supplier. Do not forage wild mushrooms without expert knowledge.
Blanch fresh mushrooms as directed by the seller and rinse before cooking. Thaw pre-cleaned frozen mushrooms in the refrigerator.
Add the mushrooms near the end and cook just until tender; prolonged cooking can make the broth more bitter.

ingredients.name: Prepared tram mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Use mushrooms cleaned and safely blanched by a trusted supplier; pre-cleaned frozen mushrooms are also suitable.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel and devein; leave small shrimp whole or chop coarsely.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Replace part of the water with strained shrimp broth if desired.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually once the soup comes to a boil.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the soup just before serving.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use to sauté the shallots and shrimp.

preparation_steps: Check the label and preparation guidance for the tram mushrooms. If fresh mushrooms have not been cleaned, ask the seller how to blanch them; never use wild mushrooms from an unknown source.
Peel and devein the shrimp, rinse briefly and drain. Mince the shallots; chop the scallions and cilantro.
Rinse the prepared mushrooms with clean water and drain. If using frozen mushrooms, thaw them in the refrigerator and discard the liquid.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots in oil until fragrant. Add the shrimp and cook just until pink, season with a little fish sauce, then transfer to a bowl.
Pour the water into the pot and bring it to a boil, skimming off any foam. Season with salt and the remaining fish sauce; keep the broth light and delicate.
Add the prepared tram mushrooms and simmer for 4–5 minutes. Return the shrimp to the pot and cook until fully done.
Turn off the heat and finish with scallions, cilantro and pepper. Serve hot with steamed rice.
canh-nam-tram-phu-quoc.media_alt_text: A bowl of clear Phu Quoc tram mushroom soup with purple-brown mushrooms, fresh shrimp, scallions and cilantro.
